_description: Pillar 3 — Naming (per-pillar rule model). Loaded by pre-write-guard.sh at runtime. Homes R-04, R-10, R-20, R-27, R-28, R-60 (R-27/R-28 categorized C3 — the canonical home != category divergence). _rules[] is the per-pillar rule SoT (each object carries home/category/surface?/status).

_design_notes.evolution_protocol: R-37 documentary lockstep — naming-rules.json + pre-write-guard.sh move in one commit; no write-time DENY for R-37 (git commit-boundary + librarian governance-parity-audit).

_rules.failure_mode: File written to an undocumented vault-root drifts structure; navigation guides go stale. Advisory: write proceeds; operator told to move the file or register the directory via /govern register.
_rules.rule_text: Files written to a vault-root directory must reside in a documented root. The allowlist is this rule's `known_roots` list, read at write time from the composed foundation bundle by pre-write-guard.sh; the hardcoded list in that hook is a bundle-less fallback mirror of this one and moves with it. It covers foundation-shipped system folders only; user-created top-level folders register via overlay-master path_routing extensions. A small set of top-level files is exempt from the root-must-be-a-directory rule. Adding a new foundation-shipped root requires R-10's checklist + R-37 lockstep.
_rules.known_roots_rationale: A directory belongs on this list only when a shipped surface establishes it as a foundation root: the vault-init tree, an `[F]` row in the vault CLAUDE.md structure template, the guard's own foundation-system-folder register, or a governance pillar naming it foundation-shipped. Adopter-created top-level folders register via overlay-master path_routing instead. Work qualifies on that test: the guard's own folder register and the CLAUDE.md template's [F] rows both list it.
_rules.known_roots_exclusion_rationale: Appearing in a walker exemption, orphan-exclusion or loose-schema list does not qualify a directory — those lists tolerate optional content wherever it exists and carry folders that are not roots. `Inbox/` is the worked case: it appears in several such lists, no shipped surface establishes it as a root, and it is therefore deliberately absent from known_roots.

_rules.failure_mode: New top-level directories created mid-session without schema/hook/librarian/governance entries. Produces orphan roots invisible to walkers.
_rules.rule_text: Adding a new vault-root directory requires walking the New Structure Checklist deliberately. The checklist binds CLAUDE.md, governance pillars (frontmatter-rules.json + file-type-contracts), hooks, and librarian into R-37 documentary lockstep so a new root cannot land in isolation.
checklist_items: Declare purpose — what archetype/content the directory holds
Declare consumer — which skill, hook, capability, or query parses this path
Add governance/frontmatter-rules.json#types entry + governance/file-type-contracts/<file>.json body-structure contract (the latter only if the new root carries a foundation-shipped mandatory file)

Add the root to governance/naming-rules.json :: _rules[R-04].known_roots (the SoT the guard reads from the composed bundle at write time) + rebuild the composed master; the hook's hardcoded list is only the bundle-less fallback mirror and moves with the pillar
Commit R-37 documentary lockstep — all surfaces move in one commit

enforcement_layer: promotion-pending: pre-commit hook if drift recurs
_rules.failure_mode: Silent gitignore bypass — bare-name patterns match only at repo root; deeper instances slip through.
_rules.rule_text: Gitignore patterns matching directory names at any depth must use the `**/` prefix. Bare-name patterns match only at repo root; `**/<name>/` matches anywhere in the tree. Documentary-only; promote to pre-commit hook if drift recurs.

_rules.source: governance/naming-rules.json :: _rules (SoT; home naming, category C3 — the canonical home != category divergence)
_rules.failure_mode: Plans without numeric prefix or status break librarian plan-index regeneration. Shame slugs degrade plan-index, backlog routing, and search-by-name.
_rules.rule_text: New or edited plan-root files must carry (a) an `NN-` numeric prefix on their top-level path segment AND (b) an authoritative status. The status is satisfied by any of: a `**Status:**` header bullet, YAML `status:` frontmatter, a `manifest.json` top-level `status` field, OR — for `spec.md` and `00-ideation-brief.md` — a sibling `manifest.json` carrying a top-level `status` field. spec.md/00-ideation-brief.md are manifest-derived: the manifest is the single status SoT, so an artifact carrying no inline status defers to its plan's manifest and DENYs only when the manifest carries no status either. Flat-root plans and README.md have no sibling manifest and keep the inline `**Status:**`/`status:` requirement; a `manifest.json` write keeps its OWN top-level `status`. Status values use the canonical 6-state lifecycle.status_enum; the spec-status-enum advisory rides inside R-27 (advisory; never retro-denies legacy plans). Sub-task files, handoffs, and orchestrator artifacts inherit from parent per R-28 and are NOT required to carry status. DENY at write-time.
status_acceptance: sibling manifest.json status (spec.md + 00-ideation-brief.md are manifest-derived under the single status SoT — a no-inline-status artifact defers to its plan manifest; DENY only when the sibling manifest has no status)
_rules._enforcement_scope_depth3_note: The last two globs ({plans_root}/*/*/spec.md + {plans_root}/*/*/manifest.json) extend R-27's enforcement to depth-3 sub-plan roots. A depth-3 sub-plan manifest.json is a governed peer carrying its OWN canonical status, NOT a status-derived shadow of the master; a sub-plan can be paused independently of its master, and the master sub_plans[] aggregate reflects each sub's published status. A depth-3 sub-plan spec.md is manifest-derived under the single status SoT — it defers to its sibling manifest's status rather than carrying its own. The hook substance asserts: (a) parent dir matches {plans_root}/NN-{master}/NN-{sub}/; (b) target is spec.md or manifest.json; (c) for manifest.json, status: present + value in the lifecycle.status_enum; (d) for spec.md, an inline **Status:**/YAML status: OR a sibling manifest.json status — DENY fires only when neither an inline marker nor a sibling-manifest status is present.

enforcement_layer: pre-write-guard.sh parent_plan write-time gate (DENY on depth>=3 sub-plan ROOT artifacts: spec.md / tasks.md / 00-ideation-brief.md; marker R28_DENY)
librarian plan-parent-resolve capability (read-time / reconciler drift finding — the broad sub-task-file population stays at this lane)
_rules.failure_mode: Sub-plan files at depth >= 3 without parent_plan: frontmatter are invisible to plan-tree walkers — librarian cannot resolve ancestry. PROMOTED: the sub-plan ROOT artifacts (spec.md / tasks.md / 00-ideation-brief.md) DENY at write time; the broad sub-task-file population (research notes, packets) stays a read-time reconciler drift finding, never a write block.
_rules.rule_text: Sub-task files at depth >= 3 under `{plans_root}/` must carry `parent_plan: <top-level-slug>` frontmatter. Value is the top-level plan slug (no path, no extension). Plan-root files at depth 2, handoff.md at any depth, files under tests/, and files under _orchestrator/ are EXEMPT. R-28 is the COMPLEMENT to R-27: R-27 governs the sub-plan's OWN status; R-28 governs the sub-plan's POINTER TO ITS MASTER. Both fire on depth-3 sub-plan roots, independently. PROMOTED per this rule's own rollout.promotion_mechanism: pre-write-guard DENIES a depth>=3 sub-plan ROOT artifact (spec.md / tasks.md / 00-ideation-brief.md) missing parent_plan:; escape hatch R28_ALLOW_OVERRIDE=1; the broader population remains librarian-audit advisory.
_rules.field_value_format: top-level plan slug (no path, no extension)
exemptions: Plan-root files at depth 2 (spec.md, tasks.md, handoff.md, 00-ideation-brief.md, README.md, manifest.json) — they ARE the parent
handoff.md at any depth (append-only session record)
Files under tests/ (synthetic fixtures, not plan state)
Files under _orchestrator/ (orchestrator runtime, not plan state)

rollout._description: Keep advisory at v1.0.0; promote post-v1.0.0 after 30+ days of advisory-fire data.
rollout.v1_0_0: ADVISORY at write-time (surfaces drift via librarian reconciler drift finding; no write-block).
rollout.observation_window: >= 30 days post-v1.0.0; librarian reconciler logs every R-28 advisory fire as a drift finding.
rollout.promotion_trigger: When advisory-fire data shows empirically low FP-rate (the scaffolder-emitted parent_plan correct-by-construction property), R-28 promotes to write-time DENY.
rollout.promotion_mechanism: A substance change to pre-write-guard.sh or to this rule's enforcement_layer field; does NOT require a superseding ADR (the advisory-then-promote rollout idiom is part of the rule itself).
rollout.promoted: Write-time DENY live on the sub-plan ROOT scope. Trigger verified at promotion: build-time census found 446 depth>=3 sub-plan-root artifacts with ZERO missing parent_plan (scaffolder-emitted, correct-by-construction) and 21 broad-population strays (historical deep files), which is why the DENY scope is the ROOTS population — the strays stay advisory at the reconciler lane. Promotion mechanism used: guard substance change + this enforcement_layer/tier edit, one commit, no superseding ADR (per promotion_mechanism).

_rules.failure_mode: Tags not conforming to the canonical tag grammar drift the taxonomy; tag-based navigation and graph view degrade.
_rules.rule_text: Tags must conform to the canonical tag grammar (kebab-case dimension prefixes per the tagging taxonomy). DENY at write-time on grammar violation. The substance lives at runtime against the tagging pillar's taxonomy; this is the renumbered identity of the former R-32-taxonomy.
